Data.SecondaryAudience: Lead Engineers, Security Architect, QA Lead

ToneOptions.Label: Authoritative & Precise
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Maintain an authoritative and precise tone, focusing on technical accuracy and clarity.

ToneOptions.Label: Strategic & Visionary
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Adopt a strategic and visionary tone, emphasizing architectural foresight and impact.

ToneOptions.Label: Pragmatic & Actionable
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Employ a pragmatic and actionable tone, guiding implementation and operationalization.

ToneOptions.Label: Rigorous & Comprehensive
ToneOptions.FullPhrase: Utilize a rigorous and comprehensive tone, ensuring all technical facets are covered.

GoalOptions.Label: Architectural Alignment
GoalOptions.Text: Ensure all stakeholders, especially Lead Engineers and Security Architects, understand and align with the proposed event-driven architecture for the Intelligent Debugging Assistant. This document aims to secure consensus on the core design principles and integration points, facilitating a unified development approach.

GoalOptions.Label: Technical Feasibility
GoalOptions.Text: Validate the technical feasibility of achieving sub-second response times for debugging suggestions and >90% accuracy for root cause identification within an event-driven IT services context. The goal is to provide sufficient detail for Lead Engineers to commence detailed design and for QA Leads to define robust testing strategies.

GoalOptions.Label: Security & Compliance
GoalOptions.Text: Articulate the security implications and compliance requirements for handling sensitive log and code data within the AI Assistant's event-driven data flows. This document seeks to inform the Security Architect on necessary controls and the QA Lead on security testing protocols, ensuring data integrity and privacy.

GoalOptions.Label: Operational Readiness
GoalOptions.Text: Define the operational requirements and considerations for deploying and maintaining the Intelligent Debugging Assistant with 99.9% availability. The objective is to equip Lead Engineers and QA Leads with the information needed to design for resilience, monitoring, and efficient incident response in an event-driven environment.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Technical & Performance Focus
Criteria: The document clearly defines event schemas and data contracts for all major event types.
Architectural diagrams accurately depict event producers, consumers, and message brokers.
Performance targets (sub-second response, >90% accuracy) are mapped to specific technical components.
Scalability and resilience mechanisms for the event-driven solution are explicitly detailed.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Security & Compliance Focus
Criteria: Data classification and handling procedures for ingested logs and code are clearly outlined.
Authentication and authorization mechanisms for event producers and consumers are specified.
Data encryption (in-transit and at-rest) strategies for event streams and storage are defined.
Compliance with relevant data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) is addressed for data processing.

CriteriaOptions.Label: Development & Operations Focus
Criteria: Integration points with developer IDEs and existing CI/CD pipelines are well-defined.
Monitoring and alerting strategies for event processing health and AI model performance are described.
Deployment strategies (e.g., blue/green, canary) for event-driven microservices are proposed.
Rollback procedures and disaster recovery plans for core event-driven services are considered.
